2. The case of the petitioners, as set out in the Writ Petition, in short, is as follows: The petitioners are the ex-students of various Departments of Jahangirnagar University. Anyway, on 17.04.2015, on the basis of some fake and unwarranted allegations leveled against the petitioners the Deputy Registrar (Education) of Jahangirnagar University (respondent no. 7) served notices upon them informing them that they had been expelled temporarily from the University by the respondent no.4 purportedly under Section 8 of the Discipline Board Ordinance. On 19.04.2015, the office of the respondent no.6 directed the petitioners over telephone to be present the Council Room of the University at 2.30 P.M. on the same day and accordingly, they rushed to the Council Room and appeared before the Complaint Committee at the scheduled time and were handed over the notices dated 18.04.2015 vide Memo No.8690(8). However, they denied all the allegations brought against them and gave extempore written statements as per the direction of the Complaint Committee.  3. The respondent nos.2-5 has opposed the Rule by filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition. Their case, as set out therein, in brief, is as follows: 

 5. In the Affidavit-in-Reply submitted by the petitioners, it has been averred that the Complaint Committee inquired into the allegations brought against the petitioners going beyond their jurisdiction as the Committee is empowered to inquire into the cases of sexual harassment only. As the petitioners were not provided with the copies of the inquiry report submitted by the Inquiry Committee, they did not get 'any opportunity to controvert the allegations effectively. The Complaint Committee in its report did not recommend their expulsion for life, though the Discipline Board recommended their life-long expulsion which was ultimately approved by the Syndicate of the University. As the Complaint Committee does not have the right to inquire into any allegation other than that of sexual harassment, the basis of punishment imposed upon the petitioners has no legs to stand upon. 

 7. Mr. Mohammad Faridul Islam further submits that indisputably no copies of the inquiry report submitted by the Inquiry Committee were supplied to the petitioners and that being so, they were seriously prejudiced in consequence of which they failed to controvert the allegations in an effective manner and The principle of fairness was not adhered to by the Discipline Board by its failure to provide the petitioners with the copies of inquiry report and this signal failure has resulted in a miscarriage of justice. On this point, Mr. Mohammad Faridul Islam has drawn our attention to the decision in the case of Durjoy Deb ...Vs...Khulna University of Engineering & Technology, Khulna and others reported in 66 DLR (HCD) 189. 

 8. Mr. Mohammad Faridul Islam also submits that the Complaint Committee of Jahangirnagar University was constituted in accordance with the mandate, given by the High Court Division in the case of Bangladesh National Women Lawyers' Association (BNWLA) represented by its Executive Director Mrs. Salma Ali...Vs...Government of Bangladesh, and others in Writ Petition No.5916 of 2008 (14 BLC (HCD) 694) and excepting the allegation of sexual harassment, the Complaint Committee was not authorized to inquire into the other allegations levelled against the petitioners and as the allegation of sexual harassment was not admittedly proved, the Complaint Committee clearly overstepped its authority in making 

 10. Mr. Mohammad Faridul Islam also submits that there is virtually no exhaustive disciplinary law for dealing with the misconduct of the University students and as such the respondents dealt with the alleged misconduct of the petitioners by giving them singularly inadequate time to controvert the allegations brought against them and the entire episode was orchestrated by the University Authority in an arbitrary and cavalier fashion. 

 13. Per contra, Mr. A. S. M. Abdul Mobin, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent nos.2-5, concedes that there is no exhaustive disciplinary law for the Students of Jahangirnagar University and in case of any misconduct committed by any student of the University, there is no set timeframe within which he is to show cause in response to the allegations that have been levelled against him and there is no time-bound mode of inquiry there into by the Inquiry Committee and this being the position, he has advised the University Authority to frame an exhaustive disciplinary law for the students. 

 Be that as it may, Mr. A. S. M. Abdul Mobin X submits that as there is a provision of appeal embodied in Section 51 of the Jahangirnagar University Act, 1973, the instant Rule is not maintainable. In this respect, he relies upon the decision in the case of Controller of Examinations, University of Dhaka and others ..Vs... Mahinuddin and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 305. 

 17. We do not find any definition of 'Misconduct' in the Discipline Rules of 1990 and this has been conceded to by Mr. A. S. M. Abdul Mobin. Besides, no mode of inquiry has been spelt out in the Discipline Rules of 1990. On the other hand, the Discipline Ordinance of 2009 has been kept in abeyance according to the decision of the Syndicate dated 07.04.2010 vide Annexure-'5(2)' to the Affidavit- in-Opposition. So the actual position is that the Discipline Ordinance of 2009 has been in abeyance as of now. 

 18. According to Mr. A. S. M. Abdul Mobin, with the postponement of the Discipline Ordinance of 2009 by the Syndicate on 07.04.2010, the previous Discipline Rules of 1990 automatically revived. Anyway, it transpires that the petitioners were meted out punishment as per the provisions of the Discipline Rules of 1990. In the facts and circumstances of the instant case, we find that the Discipline Ordinance of 2009 was framed by the University Authority by keeping the Discipline Rules of 1990 alive. In such view of the matter, after the postponement of the Discipline Ordinance of 2009 by the Syndicate on 07.04.2010, the question of revival of the earlier Discipline Rules of 1990 as contended by Mr. A. S. M. Abdul Mohin does not arise at all. 

 19. What is significant is that the impugned order dated 28.05.2015 (Annexure-P to the Writ Petition) is conspicuously silent about the specific law under which the petitioners were permanently expelled. Again, the order of temporary expulsion of the petitioners for misconduct dated 17.04.201 5 (Annexure-'A' to the Writ Petition) seems to be violative of Section 8 of the Discipline Board Ordinance which refers to a specific period of expulsion of a student by the Vice-Chancellor of the University. However, in view of the postponement of the Discipline Ordinance of 2009 by the University Syndicate, we find that the Discipline Rules of 1990 hold the field. As already observed, no mode of inquiry has been spelt out in the Discipline Rules of 1990. This is a great vacuum therein. The University Authority has never thought of this vacuum. Precisely speaking, this is a grey area in the field of disciplinary law for the students. So an exhaustive disciplinary law for the students of Jahangirnagar University should be made as soon as possible. 

 It is often said that malafide or bad faith vitiates, everything and a malafide act is a nullity. What is malafide? Relying on some observations of the Indian Supreme Court in some decisions, Durgadas Basu J held, "It is commonplace to state that malafides does not necessarily involve a malicious intention. It is enough if the aggrieved party establishes: (i) that :he authority making the impugned order did not apply its mind at all to the matter in question; or (ii) that the impugned order was made for a purpose or upon a ground other than what is mentioned in the order" (Ram Chandra...Vs...Secretary to the Government of W.B, AIR 1964 Cal 265). Reverting to the case in hand, it is ex-facie clear that the University Authority did not apply its mind at all in making the impugned order dated 28.05.2015. 

 It is undisputed that the petitioners preferred an appeal before the Chancellor against the impugned order dated 28.05.2015 in accordance with Section 51 of the Jahangirnagar University Act, 1973 and subsequently they withdrew the appeal and filed the instant Writ Petition under Article 102 of tile Constitution. As we have found the impugned order dated 28.05.2015 'non est' and malafide, the petitioners are entitled to invoke the writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution and by that reason, the Rule is maintainable. In this respect, the decision relied on by Mr. A. S. M. Abdul Mobin in the case of Controller of Examinations, University of Dhaka and 9thers ...Vs... Mahinuddin and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 305 does not appear to be of any avail to him in that the facts and circumstances of the instant case are distinguishable from those of the case under reference. 

 21. In view of what have been stated above and having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, we find merit in the Rule. The Rude, therefore, succeeds.
